speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing agitation and yellowing of the skin and eyes. To help me narrow down the cause, can you tell me if you have been experiencing any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behaviors, have you had any unprotected sex with new partners recently, and do you recall any recent fevers or joint pains? I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis, so please also confirm if your urine has been dark like tea or your stools pale.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I have noted your history. To further evaluate the cause of your jaundice and agitation, I need to check your liver function and screen for viral hepatitis.

REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated). Hepatitis Panel results not provided in current data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show severe liver dysfunction with significantly elevated bilirubin and transaminases, along with impaired synthetic function (low TP activity, elevated INR). Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, cocaine use, and acute onset of agitation and jaundice, I need to determine if this is viral hepatitis or acute liver failure secondary to another cause. Have you consumed any mushrooms, supplements, or acetaminophen in the last week, and have you experienced any right upper quadrant pain or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient denies significant alcohol use or acetaminophen/mushroom ingestion, which makes toxic causes less likely given the acute presentation. Given the high-risk sexual history and severe acute liver failure markers, I must confirm the viral etiology immediately.

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_A_IgM
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_Surface_Antigen
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_Core_IgM

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative results for Hepatitis A and B markers make viral hepatitis less likely, so I need to investigate other causes such as autoimmune hepatitis, Wilson's disease, or drug-induced liver injury from substances like cocaine or ecstasy. Do you have a family history of liver disease, and have you noticed any confusion, tremors, or unusual behavioral changes beyond the agitation?

REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel
REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin
REQUEST TEST: Serum_Copper

speaker: Doctor
text:
With autoimmune hepatitis and Wilson's disease effectively ruled out by normal ceruloplasmin and autoimmune panels, I must consider drug-induced liver injury or acute viral hepatitis C. Have you taken any over-the-counter medications, herbal supplements, or new recreational substances in the last two weeks?

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_C_Antibody
REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_C_RNA

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative Hepatitis C results, combined with the exclusion of A, B, autoimmune, and Wilson's disease, strongly point toward drug-induced liver injury, particularly given the history of ecstasy and cocaine use. I will order a specific screen for recreational drug metabolites and check for acute liver failure complications.

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Drug_Screen
REQUEST TEST: Ammonia_Level
REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level

speaker: Doctor
text:
The negative drug and acetaminophen screens are puzzling given the severe liver injury and negative viral/autoimmune workup. I need to rule out vascular causes like Budd-Chiari syndrome or structural issues, so I will request imaging and check for coagulopathy further.

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_CT_Scan
REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram
REQUEST TEST: Factor_V_Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal CT Scan: No evidence of Budd-Chiari syndrome; liver appears congested. Echocardiogram: Normal cardiac function, no signs of right heart failure. Factor V Activity: < 40% (reduced), consistent with severe hepatic synthetic dysfunction.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The imaging rules out vascular causes, and the severely reduced Factor V activity confirms acute liver failure with poor synthetic function. Given the exclusion of viral, autoimmune, metabolic, and common toxic causes, along with the history of recreational drug use, this presentation is most consistent with severe drug-induced liver injury, potentially from an unreported toxin or idiosyncratic reaction to substances like ecstasy.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Liver Injury
